dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: GM1 gangliosidosis type III (chronic/adult form), an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the GLB1 gene leading to deficient beta-galactosidase activity and accumulation of GM1 ganglioside in the central nervous system, presenting with a progressive movement disorder and bilateral putaminal signal change on MRI.

1. Wilson disease (ATP7B mutation, copper accumulation) — would require serum ceruloplasmin, 24-hour urinary copper, and slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings
2. Mitochondrial cytopathy (e.g., Leigh-like syndrome or POLG-related disorder) — would warrant lactate/pyruvate, muscle biopsy, and mitochondrial genetic testing
3. Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA / PKAN, PANK2 mutation) — characterised classically by the "eye of the tiger" sign in the globus pallidus, which can occasionally mimic putaminal change
